♡Family Today♡

Back to the regular week. Warm today, a noisy one tomorrow afternoon, then the nicest stretch of the month Thursday through Saturday.
  • Sep 13Bills at Houston, Jets at Tennessee — both at 1:00

In plain English The barometer is high and has stopped climbing — 30.25 today, 30.21 yesterday, a tiny move after Monday's big jump. Small moves mean low migraine risk, and that is where today sits. Tomorrow's storm will push the needle down fast through the afternoon, and a fast drop is the kind of thing that sets you off. Tomorrow is the day to watch, not today.

✶The Ledger✶

Straight losses in Houston
6
Buffalo has not won in Houston since 2006, and Josh Allen is 1–4 against the Texans. He says it is the one game on the schedule he actually looked at.

✶The National Wire✶

1

Nepal Mourns 1,300 Dead as the Search Goes On

Flags at half-staff Monday, the 13th day after the Himalayan floods. Some 5,000 are still missing, hundreds of them workers buried in hydropower tunnels.

2

Iran to Draw a “Restricted Zone” in the Gulf

Ships entering without Tehran's say-so would be sanctioned. Oil rose Monday after a weekend of strikes on shipping; the war is now past six months.

3

NATO Drills in Greenland as Europe Pledges Aid

Troops from eleven countries train there this week. Von der Leyen promised $230 million and said Greenland's future is for Greenlanders and Danes to decide.

4

Germany's Far Right Wins a State, Just Misses a Majority

AfD took 44 percent in Saxony-Anhalt, 39 of 83 seats, three short of governing alone. No mainstream party will join it.

Why it matters: since 1945 no far-right party has run a German state, on purpose — every other party refuses to work with AfD, an arrangement Germans call the firewall, and this is the closest it has come to breaking. Germany's own domestic intelligence service has labeled the party right-wing extremist. Its leaders campaign on mass deportations and friendlier ties with Russia, and one of its founders called the Nazi years a “speck of bird droppings” in a thousand years of German history. It is not the Nazi party. It is the first party since the Nazis that nearly half a German state has voted for while it talks like that.

🏈The Gridiron🏈

Five Days to Kickoff
Bills · at Houston, Sunday 1:00 on FOX, where the Texans have won six straight against Buffalo. DeMeco Ryans spent Monday on Josh Allen: nobody extends a play like him, so the rush cannot quit. Khalil Shakir has missed practice with an undisclosed injury and is expected to play; DJ Moore, in from Chicago, is the new No. 1. New left guard, and no fullback on the roster for the first time in Allen's career.
Jets · at Tennessee, Sunday 1:00 on CBS. Kenyon Sadiq, the first-round tight end, is back at practice after missing the whole preseason and will play on a short snap count. Breece Hall is on track. Geno Smith runs Frank Reich's offense; last year's Jets were the first team ever to go a season without a defensive interception. That is the bar.

⚑The Chase⚑

Nine to Go
Round two is Gateway on Sunday, a flat mile-and-a-quarter outside St. Louis. Hamlin leads Bell by twelve after his Darlington scrape; Larson, seventh and 49 back, has the most ground to make up. No eliminations means nobody is desperate yet. That changes by October.

★The Marquee★

1

Rob Reiner Wins an Emmy, Nine Months After His Death

A standing ovation Sunday for his guest turn on The Bear. Widow's Bay, canceled after one season, won eight.

2

Colbert Gets the Last Word

The canceled Late Show took the variety-writing Emmy, ending John Oliver's ten-year run in the category. The main ceremony is Monday night.

3

Bad Bunny's Halftime Show Takes Seven

The Super Bowl set was the biggest winner of the weekend's first night. Antiques Roadshow won its first ever, on the 25th nomination.

☾On This Day☾

September 8, 1966 — sixty years ago tonight, NBC aired the first episode of Star Trek. Canceled after three seasons for poor ratings; it has not been off the air since.
